owner_answers.label: What it takes to make a good team, as far as this measurement can say
owner_answers.text: On the 24 tournament-ready teams, swapping a whole Pokemon or one move moved the win rate by about 5 to 6 points, and replacing an item or an ability moved it by about 4 points, all clearly beyond battle luck. Changing the stat alignment or copying Stat Points from another real set did not show an effect above zero in either group, which is not the same as doing nothing. On the 16 search-found teams only the whole Pokemon swap and the move swap showed an effect. Every edit was a random legal value scored by its size and not its direction, with one behaviour cloning policy playing both sides against the 50 top-placing teams, so this says which parts a good team is sensitive to and not which choices make it good.

owner_answers.label: What we can say about noise
owner_answers.text: We measured battle luck by replaying each of the 40 starting teams three more times with nothing changed, 384 battles each time, and comparing every replay with the team's first score. Two scores of the same unchanged team differ by 3.40 win-rate points for tournament-ready teams and 3.73 points for search-found teams, root mean square, which is close to the 3.61 points that coin-flip arithmetic predicts for two independent scores near a 0.5 win rate over 384 battles. That luck is almost as large as the edits themselves, since a whole-Pokemon swap moved a tournament-ready team by 6.81 points before the correction and 5.90 points after it. We removed the luck by subtracting the replays' mean squared change from the edits' mean squared change and taking the square root, because a real change and independent luck add as squares. The correction works only on average over many edits, so it cannot say which single edit was real, and it cannot widen the measurement beyond one behaviour cloning policy against one pool of 50 opponent teams. It also floors a size at zero, which pushes small sizes upward, and every team scored on the same seed met the same opponent order and the same slot shuffles, so part of the luck is shared between teams.
